editorial_notes: All 43 supplied Genesis36 units and all36 supplied Genesis37 units received an initial curated pass. Every source unit has at least one retained pair. Completion means this initial pass, not exhaustive discovery of all possible references.

Genesis36:2 retains Adah/Elon/Hittite and Oholibamah/Anah/Zibeon/Hivite; Genesis26:34 instead supplies Judith/Beeri/Hittite and Basemath/Elon/Hivite. No wife renaming or ethnicity correction is invented. Genesis36:3 Basemath and28:9 Mahalath retain their shared Ishmael-and-Nebaioth relationship and different personal names.

Family-record comparisons with Chronicles concern clearly parallel Esau, Seir, royal or Edom-chief lists. They retain each record's actual names and membership. These are not credits for independently resolving every similarly spelled individual's historical identity or performing original-language verification.

Timna is Eliphaz's concubine in36:12 and Lotan's sister in36:22; Chronicles1:39 lists Chorri, Aiman, Ailath and Namna as Lotan's sons. Chief Timna in36:40 is not identified with the concubine merely by name.

The extra Korah in the Eliphaz chief list is not inserted into the earlier Eliphaz offspring list or forcibly identified with Oholibamah's Korah. Dishon, Anah and similarly named figures are not silently merged across family branches.

Genesis36:24 keeps Aiah, Onan, Onas and Iamin as supplied. No hot-springs, mule, or alternative-person interpretation is supplied for Iamin, and no appeal to an unperformed Greek/Hebrew check is made.

Genesis36:27 has four Asar sons, whereas Chronicles1:42 gives three Osar sons; Genesis36:28 Rison/Uz/Aram is not forcibly mapped to Chronicles Daison/Os/Arran. Genesis36:39 Arad differs from Chronicles Adad, and its Mehetabel/Matred son of Me-zahab notice remains additional rather than harmonized away. Zaphoim and Heram remain different supplied final-chief names.

Genesis36:31 explicitly places Edom's kings before a king reigned in Israel; the supplied Chronicles introduction lacks that explicit chronological clause. The relation to35:11 distinguishes the promise of kings to Jacob from Edom's stated royal chronology.

Genesis37:2 supplies Bilhah and Zilpah as Jacob's wives, whereas35:25-26 identifies them as Rachel's and Leah's slave women. Neither description is erased. The evil report is Joseph's reported action, without claiming its contents or truth are established.

The dreams, Jacob's rebuke and family interpretation, brothers' envy, and later narrator's explicit dream recollection are distinguished. Benjamin is absent on the first Egypt visit and present on the later one. The bowing links do not claim that every sun, moon or star figure receives a separately reported literal fulfilment; Rachel's earlier death remains visible.

Reuben's proposed pit confinement averts immediate killing but does not accomplish the narrated intention to restore Joseph to his father. His later empty-pit discovery and speech remain distinct from that intention.

Genesis37:28 retains twenty pieces of gold, Midianite merchants, Ishmaelites and an unforced reading of the pronoun they. Genesis37:36 names Midianites as sellers to Potiphar;39:1 names Ishmaelites. Later Joseph/Stephen/psalm retrospective statements are attributed as later statements and do not silently resolve the different actor descriptions.
Potiphar remains Pharaoh's eunuch and chief cook in both37:36 and39:1; no common replacement title such as captain of the guard is introduced.

The planned beast story, brothers' actual garment presentation, Jacob's false death conclusion, and Judah's later report of Jacob's speech remain separate narrative levels. The garment really is Joseph's; that does not make the inferred death true.

The goat-and-garment comparison distinguishes goat skins in the earlier deception of Isaac from goat blood in the deception of Jacob. The Tamar recognition parallel concerns Judah's identifying possessions, not objects originally belonging to Tamar; no linguistic derivation or divine-punishment claim is made.

Jacob's Hades language, refusal of comfort, and later rekindled spirit remain supplied wording; no eternal-separation doctrine or literal resurrection is inferred. The shorter psalm sale summary is not assigned exclusively to either individual sale transaction.

Same-chapter links are explicitly labelled and concern named family branches, genealogy frames, commission and response, changing destinations, a tracked garment, intentions and outcomes, or contrasted knowledge states. No fixed pair quota was imposed.

candidate_exclusions.reason: Removed the separate repeated-Korah identity candidate. The retained family-versus-chief-list comparison records the extra Korah without depending on whether the entries denote one person.

Removed a candidate that could imply the adjacent Dishon mentions establish a single person despite another Dishon in the larger Seir list. The retained Chronicles reference is explicitly a parallel-record comparison, not a resolved personal-identity table.
Did not equate Onan, Onas, Ana or Iamin; the same-chapter Zibeon heading supplies the supported branch reference without forcing those identities.
Did not force Rison/Uz/Aram into Daison/Os/Arran as resolved individual identities. The explicit same-chapter Rison branch is retained instead.
Did not claim the supplied many-coloured tunic and Tamar's wrist-length garment are the same description or offer an unperformed original-language word comparison.
Did not add a place-name-only Dothan/Dothaim pairing without examining that additional passage in this run.
No sale-price or Judas/Judah identity or unqualified typological equivalence is claimed; the source gold amount is preserved.

editorial_notes.note: Hirah remains the Adullamite and, in12, Judah's shepherd. Shua is named in the marriage and called Judah's wife in12. The comparison with1Chronicles2:3 preserves that verse's Shua's daughter wording, and does not settle the naming difference by replacing either source.

Er's unspecified evil is not supplied with an invented offence. Onan's stated refusal to give seed to his brother and the narrator's judgment remain in their stated context. The later Deuteronomy and Ruth links compare the preservation of a dead man's family/name without treating every kinship arrangement or legal detail as identical.

Tamar's seeing that Shelah was grown but not given to her is attributed to the narrator; Judah's later more-in-the-right comparison is his acknowledgement. Judah's punitive burning order is not labelled a divine command or a legal sentence independently verified outside the narrative.

Ainan, ring, necklace, staff and the widowhood garments retain the supplied terms. The roadside assumption and local men's replies remain attributed; no temple/cultic occupation or unreported identity is invented. The pledge's evidentiary role is grounded in the repeated three objects and Judah's recognition.

The hand with the scarlet thread and the actual sequence of emergence are distinguished. Perez and Zerah retain their names in Genesis/Matthew; no critical-language name derivation, birthright transfer, or equation with Rebekah's delivery is claimed. The later elders explicitly name Perez, Tamar and Judah in Ruth4:12.

Joseph, Egypt and Potiphar identify the purchase connection, while Midianite and Ishmaelite seller labels remain as supplied. No unreported identification of merchant groups or reconstruction of every transfer is offered. Pharaoh's eunuch and chief cook are not replaced with familiar titles from another edition.

The narrator's God-given presence/prosperity and successive human entrusting are distinguished from Laban/Jacob's earlier claims. Household master, jailer, Pharaoh and Daniel's chief eunuch remain different officials/settings. The bread exception from the household is not inserted into the prison account.

The woman's repeated demands, seizure and Joseph's refusal/flight are kept distinct from her contrary accusation. Her reported outcry is not inserted as the narrator's stated cause of flight. The master's anger is reported without specifying an unreported inner belief or exclusive object of anger. The later law against adultery is Exodus20:13 in this edition.
The supplied Greek/Septuagint Psalm numbering104 is retained. Fetters, testing and release are details of the Psalm's later retelling; they are not inserted into the literal Genesis39:20 wording.

The officials' offences are unspecified. Chief cupbearer, chief baker, chief jailer and chief cook retain their supplied descriptions without a newly asserted identity between offices. The paired dreams occur in one night, and Joseph's divine-interpretation declaration is compared with his later answer and Daniel's declaration without asserting that all dreams universally predict events.

The vine has three branches; the baker has three baskets of coarse bread, not a silently substituted white-basket description. The narrator's interpreted-rightly wording in16 is retained. Joseph assigns three days to each set; the birthday review, restoration and hanging are recorded as outcomes. Removal of the head and birds eating flesh are stated in the interpretation; the brief outcome verse is not expanded into a separately detailed eyewitness report of each element.

Joseph's stolen-from-the-Hebrews' land and innocence statements remain his speech, contextualized by the earlier pit/sale and refusal/false-accusation narrative. No universal sinlessness, unreported prayer, or condemnation of asking a person for help is inferred. The cupbearer's forgetting is not attributed to God, and his later offence remembrance is not narrowed to one unreported meaning.

editorial_notes.note: The dream, Pharaoh's retelling, Joseph's interpretation and subsequent fulfilment remain distinct. Preserve cows, reed grazing, ears on one stalk, ugly/lean versus fair/choice animals, and wind-blighted ears. No compass direction is inserted for the wind. Two full years is retained without an independent absolute chronology.

The cupbearer's offence is not newly defined as only his forgetting Joseph or given an invented offence description. Chief cook, jailer, fortress and custody wording is preserved without a new equation of every official title.

Retain the answer-bringing-deliverance wording, the one-dream declaration, and the truth/haste formulation of the repeated dream. Joseph's divine attribution, Pharaoh's Spirit-of-God commendation and Stephen's retrospective summary retain their own speakers and wording. No new original-language collation, medical explanation of dreams or Egyptian historical reconstruction is claimed.

The proposed fifth of abundant-year produce and later fifth-part land ordinance are compared as distinct arrangements. The implementation passage explicitly shows collection/storage but does not repeat the exact fraction. Ring, fine linen, golden collar, second chariot and herald retain the supplied details without an invented proclamation or ceremonial etymology. Grain like sea-sand remains a comparison, not a measured inventory.

The sold righteous man's rise from pit/bonds to authority over rulers is labelled a narrative allusion corresponding to Joseph's elevation. Wisdom does not name that man in the retained verses, and the pair does not supply independent Egyptian historical data.

Retain Psonthomphanech, Asenath, Potiphera and Heliopolis. Potiphera is not equated with Joseph's earlier master Potiphar. Manasseh remains the firstborn and Ephraim the second; later crossed-hand blessing does not change their birth order. Joseph's naming explanations remain his speech, not a newly verified etymological study or a claim that he never again remembered his father.

The seven abundant years and seven famine years are kept distinct. Egypt's bread, ensuing hunger and granary sales remain visible beside the wider famine summary and the later two-years-plus-five report. No unreported modern geographical extent, absolute date or exhaustive shortage chronology is assigned.

Benjamin is a son of Rachel alongside Joseph, but Jacob's no-more/dead/alone-left language remains his or the brothers' reported perspective. The narrator shows both Joseph and detained Simeon alive. The stated journey fear is sickness and the grief destination Hades; neither is silently replaced with another edition's wording. Jacob's Rachel-focused two-son grief is not made into a denial that his other children exist.

Ten brothers first bow before the grain ruler; this is compared with the remembered dreams without claiming every detail of both visions is enacted at this one visit. Preserve tracks-of-the-country accusation and health-of-Pharaoh wording. Spying is Joseph's accusation, while the narrator records grain purchasing; it is not a verified fact about the brothers.

The initial one-sent/others-held proposal and revised one-held/others-return arrangement remain distinct. Three-day custody and third-day speech retain their supplied sequence. The brothers' later reported warning, release and trade terms are compared without turning all reports into verbatim identical quotations.

The confession supplies Joseph's ignored begging, which the earlier pit scene does not quote. Reuben's earlier warning and later blood-accountability protest are related without a claim that Joseph actually died. The present guilt interpretation and Judah's later cup-crisis interpretation remain attributed speech rather than an independently pronounced divine causal verdict. The earlier target retains twenty pieces of gold and its stated trader identities; no new resolution of every trading pronoun is imposed.

An interpreter conceals Joseph's understanding; no additional spoken-language identification is supplied. The two private weeping scenes retain their different immediate narrative contexts. Simeon's selection and later release are recorded without an invented personal motive for choosing him.

Joseph's order explains the returned silver to the reader; the brothers' anxious God-question and steward's treasure/payment reassurance remain their different reported interpretations. Preserve one sack at the first lodging discovery, every sack at home, and the collective later lodging report without inventing a sequence to harmonize them. The second journey's restored-payment order is a separate narrated repetition.

Reuben's offer involving his two sons and Judah's later personal surety are distinct proposals. No approval of killing Reuben's sons is inferred. Later retelling of Jacob's grief is not substituted for the actual earlier wording.

editorial_notes.note: Distinguish narrated family disclosure from later reports of questions and promised care. Do not present added wording in the later reports as a verbatim quotation printed in the earlier scene.

Keep resin, honey, spices, stacte, terebinth nuts and nuts, the invocation my God, and drank and became drunk exactly as supplied. No substitute ingredient list, divine title or drinking description is inserted.

The earlier account has one brother discovering silver at the lodging and all bundles displayed before their father; the later report describes each man's silver at the lodging. Both supplied accounts are quoted without harmonizing their details.

The steward's divine-treasure explanation and the narrator's account of Joseph restoring the money remain distinct. No miraculous deposit is asserted. Do not independently assign the blessing speaker in verse28. Egyptian aversion to Hebrews at table and later aversion to shepherds retain distinct objects.

The narrator explicitly records the cup's placement on Joseph's order. Theft and divination allegations remain reported claims, and Judah's confession does not establish an actual cup theft or independently identify the precise iniquity he means.

The severe search declarations are compared with their distinct hidden-object histories: Rachel actually stole the idols; the cup was planted on Joseph's order. Neither declaration is treated as a fulfilled death sentence.

Joseph's reported death remains a family belief while he is present alive. Rachel's two sons do not erase Jacob's other wives or sons. Preserve the supplied pronoun in verse22 without resolving it independently, and retain sickness and Hades wording in the paternal warnings.

Judah's personal surety and proposed substitution are compared with his earlier proposal to sell Joseph. The contrast concerns his stated proposals; no unspoken motive, complete inner transformation or specialist theological judgment is claimed.

critical_checks: The final file contains135 retained pairs, not the earlier137-pair draft. The author's two removed ambiguous Korah/adjacent-Dishon comparisons are not counted as audited retained pairs or new reviews.
The Genesis26,28 and36 marriage records preserve Judith/Basemath, Adah/Oholibamah and Mahalath/Basemath wording and Hittite/Hivite descriptions without invented renamings or uniform ethnic labels.

The Chronicles comparisons are labelled parallel records, not an independently established one-to-one identity table. Ragouel/Reuel, Lotan's additional sons and Timna's sister relationship, variant Seir branches, and Asar's four versus Osar's three sons remain explicit.

Korah in Eliphaz's chief list is compared with the different earlier family list without inserting him among its births or identifying him with Oholibamah's son. The adjacent Dishon and other repeated-name branches are not forced into a new harmonization.
Genesis36:24 retains Aiah, Onan, Onas, Iamin and beasts of burden without a new mules, hot springs or personal-identity interpretation.

The royal lists retain Balak/Beor/Dennaba, Hadad/Adad, Samlah/Samaa, Shaul/Saul and Arad/Adad forms as supplied. No unreported identity with a similarly named Moabite king or the book of Job is asserted.

Genesis36:31's before-an-Israelite-king notice is not falsely inserted into the supplied Chronicles introduction. Genesis36:39's additional wife/ancestry notice remains distinct from Chronicles, and final chiefs Zaphoim/Heram are not declared the same person.
Territorial references are supported by the actual Seir/Horite/Edom wording and Joshua's quoted divine retrospective; no precise modern site, border or date is newly established.

Joseph's17 and30 age markers are retained without allocating every intervening episode. Bilhah/Zilpah wife wording and their earlier slave-woman wording remain as supplied; no inference about the truth of Joseph's evil report is added.

The dream links use explicit later recollection and actual bowing scenes. The mother difficulty is preserved alongside Rachel's reported death and confirmed maternity; no substitute mother or unreported parental bowing is invented.
The Luke2:19 comparison is parental retention of extraordinary reports in read context, not an assertion of direct quotation or identical events.
The unnamed man remains a man. Shechem/Dothan and Hebron settings are retained without turning the grazing location into a proven purchased plot or an exact route.

Reuben's immediate intervention and stated restoration intention are distinguished from the unaccomplished return. Judah's later offer is a contrasting action, not a declaration that the earlier sale was innocent.

Genesis37:28 has twenty pieces of gold in the supplied text. Midianite and Ishmaelite labels and Potiphar's eunuch/chief-cook title are preserved without substituting familiar silver, Medanite, or captain-of-the-guard wording.

The beast-death story and Jacob's inference are distinguished from the narrator's sale account. Recognition of a tunic versus Judah's objects has different resulting conclusions; neither is turned into a new divine-punishment doctrine.

Joseph's preservation/providence speeches remain attributed and do not excuse the brothers' murderous intent. Jacob's Hades language and later rekindled spirit are retained without a new postmortem doctrine or an assertion that Joseph actually died.

confirmed_distinctions: Genesis38:2 and38:12 name Shua as Judah's wife; Chronicles2:3 calls the Canaanite mother Shua's daughter. The comparison retains the difference rather than silently rewriting Genesis. Chronicles' Shelon and Genesis' Shelah remain supplied forms in the actual texts.

Tamar is initially Er's wife and Judah's daughter-in-law, later the mother of Judah's Perez and Zerah. The later parentage does not replace the initial marriage, and Judah's comparative acknowledgment is not made a blanket moral verdict on every action.

The links to Deuteronomy25:5-6 concern brother-in-law duty and preserving the dead man's name; Ruth4:10 has a comparable family-preservation aim with different kinship arrangements. The records are not treated as identical legal circumstances or as modern legal advice.

The Onan rationales retain the narrator's stated motive of withholding seed from his brother and the subsequent judgment. Er's wrongdoing remains unspecified, and no universal claim about unrelated sexual situations is invented.

Hirah remains Judah's shepherd in the supplied Genesis text. Ainan, Chasbi, Timnah, the veil and widowhood garments retain their supplied wording. Neither Judah's assumption nor the local men's reported denial becomes an independent narrator statement about Tamar's occupation.
The ring, necklace and staff are Judah's pledged objects, subsequently used for recognition; the young-goat payment attempt is distinct from that retained pledge.

The supplied Exodus20:13 is the adultery prohibition. The comparison to Joseph's refusal does not claim that he quotes the later written Decalogue. Genesis20:6 involves God's prevention of touching another man's wife and remains distinct in circumstances and speaker.

The woman's sexual initiative, repeated solicitations and seizure are narrator-level events. Her later reports assign initiative to Joseph; their allegations and claimed outcry are not substituted for the narrator's account. The differing quoted proposals in39:14 and39:17 remain distinct.

The master's anger follows his wife's report; its exact object is not separately specified. His imprisonment of Joseph is reported as the next event without inventing a trial, belief statement or unstated motive.

Potiphar remains eunuch and chief cook;37:36 Midianites and39:1 Ishmaelites are retained without a merged merchant identity. The chief jailer, chief cook and Pharaoh are not treated as the same official.

Joseph's trust in the household and prison is distinguished from his later authority under Pharaoh; the earlier bread exception is not inserted into the prison account. The psalm's iron/fetters details remain a later depiction rather than unreported wording inserted into39:20.
Daniel1:9 names the chief eunuch and Joseph39:21 the chief jailer. The parallel is God-given favour before distinct officials, not a shared person or identical institutional setting.

Joseph attributes dream explanation to God in40:8; the supplied41:16 says no deliverance-bringing answer without God. Daniel2:27-28 likewise contrasts human interpreters with God's disclosure. None is recast as independent personal magic or used to equate the royal dreams.

The baker's interpreted-rightly wording is preserved before the narrated outcomes; it is not silently changed to another edition's favourably wording or treated as an outcome already observed. Coarse bread, three baskets and three branches retain the supplied interpretation terms.

The predicted three-day restoration and hanging are connected with the narrated birthday outcomes. The baker's dream food and predicted flesh remain different objects of the birds' eating; the final account does not separately narrate every predicted detail of head removal or birds.

Joseph's claim of being stolen and unjustly confined is read against the earlier sale and false-accusation narrative, without resolving every actor pronoun or merchant label. The cupbearer's forgetting Joseph does not mean God forgot him. His later offence language is kept in its own reported speech.

required_corrections.issue: The phrase resumes the meal implies eating had already begun before Joseph withdrew. The narrator orders bread set out at43:31 and then describes service at43:32. Retain the restraint/disclosure contrast while correcting this sequence.
required_corrections.replace_rationale_with: Joseph restrains himself and orders bread set out here, whereas the later disclosure begins when he can no longer bear those standing beside him and sends others away.

required_corrections.issue: The existing rationale changes Jacob's declared condition from discovery of the gods with someone to whoever has stolen them. The search-and-discovery condition matters, particularly because the idols are not found and Rachel actually stole them while the later cup is planted.
required_corrections.replace_rationale_with: Jacob likewise pronounces death if Laban's gods are found with someone, without knowing Rachel stole them; the brothers do not know of the planted cup, so the hidden objects have different origins.

editorial_findings.finding: Reported questions, the added care assurance and the see-my-face warning remain reported words. The rationales do not assert that the earlier narrated exchange printed those additional clauses verbatim.

Narrated Joseph-commanded placement is separated from the brothers' ignorance, feared enslavement, steward's God-given-treasure reassurance, theft allegations and Judah's guilt statement. One-sack lodging discovery, all-bundles home discovery and the collective later lodging report remain visibly different; no independent transaction or miraculous-deposit reconstruction is imposed.

The supplied my-God invocation, ambiguous blessing speaker, distinct Egyptian aversions and drank-and-became-drunk wording remain intact. Benjamin's later exceptional gift really is three hundred pieces of gold and five robe changes in this edition. Maternal grouping is not substituted for a precise seating order.

After correcting the earlier declaration's condition, the search-declaration parallel is supported.
